As of 240 AM EST Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...A series of cold fronts bring the potential for two 
waves of isolated to scattered showers today. Otherwise, mild 
temperatures remain through this afternoon with dropping 
temperatures late. 

Fairly quiet weather-wise across the forecast area this morning. 
Nighttime microphysics satellite imagery shows some passing mid-high 
clouds, though they should scatter out over the next few hours. 
Observations near the coast of ern/SE VA and NE NC also depict some 
patchy ground fog. This is likely due to the higher dew points and 
calm winds. Most guidance does not develop widespread fog and the 
current thinking is it remains patchy through sunrise. 

A large upper trough and associated sfc low and cold front will 
bring the potential for a few rounds of isolated to widely scattered 
showers today. The first round, where PoPs are 20-30%, occurs this 
morning with an initial vorticity lobe and shortwave aloft. The late 
morning and early afternoon hours then look to be dry for most. 
Clouds are also expected to briefly scatter out during this time, 
allowing for one last day of mild temps. Forecast highs are 
generally in the mid to upper 60s, with a few ~70 F readings 
possible in SE VA and NE NC. The second round of showers follows 
along the cold front late this afternoon and evening. This is when a 
few heavier/stronger cores could develop given steep lapse rates and 
cool temps aloft. This combination allows for up to ~500 J/kg of sfc-
based CAPE. In addition, can't rule out some sporadic lightning 
strikes or small hail in the heaviest cores. The best potential for 
this late-day activity is from the nrn Piedmont into the nrn 
portions of the RIC metro, the Northern Neck, and Eastern Shore. 
However, slight chc PoPs extend roughly to the NC/VA border. These 
showers won't be efficient rainfall producers and still don't expect 
much in the way of measurable rainfall. Totals up to a tenth of an 
inch are possible, but this would be highly localized. Gusty NW 
winds overspread the area late tonight into early Friday behind the 
fronts. Overnight lows generally in the mid 40s and, despite the 
cold advection, went a few degrees above the NBM given the likely-
mixed BL and lingering clouds. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Much cooler temperatures arrive Friday into early 
next week with below freezing overnight temperatures likely inland.

An anomalously strong (-2 to -3 st dev) upper trough settles over 
the area Friday into the weekend. Following the initial push of cold 
advection behind the cold front, this trough will allow for chilly 
temps at least through early next week. Highs Friday range from the 
low-mid 50s N/NW to mid-upper 50s S/SE, under partly and mostly 
sunny skies, respectively. The coolest night of the season so far is 
likely on the way Friday night, though there is some disagreement 
across the guidance on exactly how cold it gets. Most of the hi-res 
and statistical corrections show widespread lows in the low-mid 30s, 
while the NBM is chillier. A continuing N-NW wind, especially near 
the coast, could prevent ideal radiating conditions from developing. 
Regardless if widespread readings below freezing occur, it'll still 
be quite chilly given the breeze. There is not enough confidence in 
any Freeze Watches for Friday night at this time. Highs Saturday 
will be more typical of winter, with temps only peaking the in the 
low-mid 50s. Portions of the lower MD Eastern Shore could struggle 
to get out of the 40s. Continued cold advection, a compressed 
pressure gradient, and a well-mixed BL will allow for gusty NW winds 
for most of the day...to 20-25 mph inland and 25-30 mph near the 
coast and on the Eastern Shore.

The coolest overnight temps are expected Saturday and Sunday nights. 
This is when widespread (away from the immediate coast) overnight 
freezes are likely. Lows inland generally in the upper 20s to lower 
30s, with mid to upper 30s at the immediate coast. Freeze Watches 
(and eventually Freeze Warnings) are likely for localities still in 
the growing season during this period, though it's a bit early to 
issue these being mostly >48 hrs out. Daytime highs Sunday into 
early next week look to remain in the 50s with potentially a modest 
warming trend by mid-late week. Despite the cool temps, there should 
be plenty of sunshine. Winds also gradually relax, but remain a bit 
breezy near the coast.
